To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

resilience is a developmental process, not a fixed characteristic; it is a process of good adaptation within the context of significant adversity, not an absence of problems; and it can be studied in any context, not just in the context of extreme adversity.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
resilience is the capacity of a system to absorb disturbance and reorganize while undergoing change so as to still retain essentially the same function, structure, identity, and feedback.
resilience processes are adaptive systems that enable people to overcome adversity and to thrive.
the field of resilience research is now in a fifth wave of scientific inquiry that is building on the foundations of the previous waves.
The main takeaway from our work is that
resilience is not a rare special ability that belongs to a select few "super kids," nor is it an unattainable goal.
resilience is not simply a matter of "bouncing back" from adversity.
resilience is not a rare individual quality but rather an emergent property of the person and their ecology that is shaped by the transactional processes of development.
